clue.text: Baronet comprehends curve in graph

indicators.note: to comprehend is also to include or take in, so one word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: Bart is the standard abbreviation for a baronet
an arch is a curved structure

explanation.surface: A titled gentleman understands the shape of a line plotted on a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram of bars whose heights show quantities is one familiar kind of graph.

clue.text: Invoice for advertisement

blocks.note: first meaning: a statement of charges owed
second meaning: a poster or placard put up in public

explanation.surface: Someone is charging money for placing a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a demand for payment and a printed public notice, as in bill posters.

clue.text: Over top of dish, sprinkle a pimiento

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: re means concerning, over a matter
opening letter of the word
to pepper is to sprinkle or scatter

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: scatter chopped pimiento across the top of the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimiento is a sweet red capsicum, the mild fruit used for stuffing olives.

clue.text: Where one may see aircraft hover when guarding river

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it protectively, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to hang in the air is to hover
as can mean when
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Planes are spotted hovering above a river they seem to patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangars are the large sheds at airfields in which planes are housed and serviced.

clue.text: Astronomical instrument I operated after work, getting excited close in

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer runs the observatory equipment after the day job, growing thrilled as something nears.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses only the letters of 'I operated' and 'close'; 'after work' fills out the surface rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dish antenna that gathers radio waves from space, used by astronomers to study distant objects.

clue.text: Approach and stop Bill nicking lettuce

indicators.note: nicking is stealing, so one word pockets the other and holds it inside

blocks.note: a bill passed by Parliament becomes an Act, so the two are linked
cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill is collared while pinching a lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; here it is a draft law, which on passing becomes an Act.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to go up to them and detain them, typically boldly or aggressively.

clue.text: Bore gifts

blocks.note: first meaning: the inside diameter of a gun barrel
second meaning: a person's abilities or quality

explanation.walkthrough: Bore reads as a verb, carried presents; it is the noun for a barrel's width, and gifts are talents.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the internal diameter of a firearm and also the standard of someone's talent or worth.

clue.text: Frequently in temper, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head, the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: to temper is to moderate or soften

explanation.surface: Someone is regularly in a rage and loses their cool.
explanation.walkthrough: Temper looks like a noun, anger; it is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently are direct synonyms, both meaning many times or regularly.

clue.text: Where one may be employed to follow directions to the letter?

definitions.text: Where one may be employed to follow directions to the letter?

blocks.clueFragment: Where one may be employed to follow directions to the letter?
blocks.note: surface reading: a workplace for someone who obeys instructions exactly

blocks.clueFragment: Where one may be employed to follow directions to the letter?
blocks.note: setter's reading: an office team that takes dictation and produces letters, keying them word for word

explanation.walkthrough: To the letter suggests exact obedience; it also means producing correspondence, which is what an office of typists did.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a group of typists in an office who typed up letters and documents dictated by others.

clue.text: Promoter in Belgian city, put out ...

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A promoter in a Belgian city has been displaced; the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicity agent is employed to promote a client and get them favourable attention in the media.

clue.text: Left port heavily loaded

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left
Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship departed from harbour carrying a heavy cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden describes something weighed down, burdened or carrying a full cargo.

clue.text: Forty made off stand-in spinner?

blocks.note: a double stands in for an actor
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: Someone ran away with forty items from an understudy who spins.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts, the top segment of the board is 20, and its outer ring scores double: forty points.
explanation.definitionFit: Double top is the darts name for the doubled twenty segment, worth forty points.

clue.text: Scary for one balanced in tree

indicators.note: something scary shakes you up, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous climber finds it frightening to keep balance up in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This conifer, native to the Middle East mountains, is a large evergreen tree with spreading horizontal branches.

clue.text: .... feelers, tentatively, about a member getting a small PR gift?

indicators.note: tentative feelers move uncertainly, so the letters are tried in a new order
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: an agent puts out feelers to an MP who receives a token gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A free sample is a small amount of a product handed out at no cost to promote it.

clue.text: Retort made by sapper about one job

indicators.note: about means going around, so the engineers' letters wrap the rest

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
the Roman numeral for one
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A military engineer comes back with a sharp reply about a particular task.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the British Army corps whose soldiers are sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, clever counter-reply, so it is a sharp retort in conversation.

clue.text: Solve first of conundrums humorist raised

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
Edward Lear, the Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks
raised means up

explanation.surface: A comic writer is asked to crack a riddle he has brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a mystery is to explain or resolve it, the phrasal sense of solving something.

clue.text: Alter back row

blocks.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Change the back row, as of seating or a team line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to change the order or position of things, so to alter them.

clue.text: A girl failing to finish after onset of eye complaint

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so only the opening letter counts
a word that fails to finish loses its final letter

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
taken as written
Rachel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman drops out of a race when an eye problem begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl must lose her last letter; 'after' puts the opening of eye in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here is a medical ailment, and a pain in the ear is a common minor one.

clue.text: Artist in country, first to expose sham

indicators.note: in places one word inside another
the first of the next word means just its opening letter is used

blocks.note: Chad is a country in central Africa
RA, a Royal Academician
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An artist abroad is the first to unmask a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, so it is crossword shorthand for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a show put on to keep up appearances, hence a sham.

clue.text: A whirlwind ripped a door half off

definitions.note: the article goes with the definition

indicators.note: with half taken off, only the first half of the word remains

blocks.note: ripped means torn
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A violent storm tore a door partly off its hinges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violently rotating column of air, the most destructive kind of whirlwind.

clue.text: Playboy's trendy, earns large amounts

blocks.note: a rake is a playboy, and the apostrophe-s stands for is
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable playboy makes a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake it in is an idiom for making a lot of money, gathering it up in quantity.

clue.text: Film brutish man with fireworks

blocks.note: a brutish man is called an animal
crackers are small explosive fireworks

explanation.surface: A thuggish man is setting off fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal Crackers is a 1930 Marx Brothers comedy film, adapted from their stage musical.

clue.text: Hidden pub on outskirts of Esher

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, first and last

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A secluded pub on the edge of Esher, a commuter town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner means inward and private, as in inner feelings, so concealed or hidden from view.

clue.text: Tinned meat from Belgian town, third in hamper

indicators.note: the third in a word is its third letter only

blocks.note: Spa is the Belgian resort town that gave its name to spas
third letter of the word

explanation.surface: Canned meat brought back from a Belgian town, packed in a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of canned luncheon meat, famous since the Second World War.

clue.text: Fruit that might go off?

blocks.note: surface reading: a piece of fruit that could turn rotten
setter's reading: a tropical fruit whose name is also slang for a hand grenade, which explodes

explanation.walkthrough: Go off suggests spoiling, as fruit does; it really means exploding, since soldiers nicknamed the grenade after this fruit for its segmented shape.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tropical fruit, and in military slang a hand grenade, which can literally detonate.

clue.text: Lad out of bed by the sound of it, first thing?

indicators.note: says we want the spelling of a phrase that merely sounds like the words given

blocks.note: a lad is a son, and one out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A boy is awake very early in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunup is dawn, and first thing means early in the morning, at the start of the day.

clue.text: Took home academic after loss of face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so losing it removes the opening letter

blocks.note: learned means scholarly, academic

explanation.surface: A scholar carried something home after a humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Take-home pay is what you earn, so took home means received as wages.

clue.text: Different in Lent, mass given by early Archbishop of Canterbury

indicators.note: made different, the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church service during the fasting season is led by a medieval archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Anselm was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1093 to 1109 and was later canonised as a saint.
